title: Maximum Length of Pair Chain
summary: Given an array of n pairs where each pair consists of two integers and the first integer is less than the second, find the longest chain of pairs where each subsequent pair's first integer is greater than the previous pair's second integer.
statement: Given an array of n pairs where each pair consists of two integers and the first integer is less than the second, find the longest chain of pairs where each subsequent pair's first integer is greater than the previous pair's second integer. The pairs can be selected in any order, but not all pairs need to be used.
constraints: 1 <= len(pairs) <= 1,000; every pair [a,b] has a < b.
A pair may follow another only when its first value is strictly greater than the previous second value.
hints: The pair finishing earliest leaves the most room for all later pairs.
Sort by right endpoint and greedily take each compatible pair.
Track the last selected end; accept when the next start is greater.
Replacing any first choice by the earliest-finishing available pair cannot reduce the remaining options.
editorial: Replacing any first choice by the earliest-finishing available pair cannot reduce the remaining options.

tests.explanation: Choose [1,2] followed by [3,4] for a chain of length two.
All three pairs form a valid increasing chain.
